cues.en: Mike: I would like to continue the discussion of these regression coefficients, these beta values, in particular, how to interpret them
cues.zh: Mike：繼續討論迴歸係數、beta 值，尤其是如何解讀，

cues.en: and the difficulties with interpreting them.
cues.zh: 以及解讀的困難。

cues.en: And that's going to motivate a standardization of these regression coefficients, and then of course, I will show you how to actually do that standardization.
cues.zh: 這會帶出迴歸係數標準化的動機，當然也會示範如何實際標準化。

cues.en: So I haven't been using this term before, unstandardized betas, but it turns out that the beta coefficients that you get from the regression model,
cues.zh: 之前沒用過「未標準化 beta」這個詞，但從迴歸模型得到的 beta 係數，

cues.en: so the raw output of the regression model, those are called unstandardized beta regressions.
cues.zh: 也就是原始輸出，稱為未標準化 beta 係數。

cues.en: And you'll see in this video why we call them that.
cues.zh: 這支影片會看到為什麼如此稱呼。

cues.en: Okay, so I'd like to go back to this equation that I showed in a previous video.
cues.zh: 回到先前展示的方程式。

cues.en: This was the one about, you know, the effects of sleeping and studying on exam performance.
cues.zh: 就是睡眠與讀書對考試表現影響的例子。

cues.en: But that doesn't really matter so much.
cues.zh: 不過，那其實沒那麼重要。

cues.en: We just need a model to work with here.
cues.zh: 只需要一個可用的模型。

cues.en: What I would like you to do is pause the video and make a statement to yourself about how exactly to interpret this beta coefficient.
cues.zh: 希望你暫停影片，自己說明，這個 beta 係數究竟該如何解讀。

cues.en: So what is the exact interpretation of beta one?
cues.zh: beta1 的確切解讀是什麼？

cues.en: Okay, did you do it?
cues.zh: 你有做嗎？

cues.en: Did you remember it?
cues.zh: 還記得嗎？

cues.en: Maybe you had to check back your notes from a previous lecture, which is totally fine.
cues.zh: 也許需要回頭查看先前筆記，完全沒問題。

cues.en: So the interpretation of beta one is the change in exam performance score, whatever units this is in,
cues.zh: beta1 表示考試分數的變化，不論分數使用什麼單位，

cues.en: for a one-unit change in the amount of sleep.
cues.zh: 對應睡眠量改變一個單位。

cues.en: So the amount of sleep, which we measure, you know, if we measure this in hours, then it would be for one hour of extra sleep, how much does your exam score change, okay?
cues.zh: 如果睡眠以小時計，就是每多睡一小時，考試分數會改變多少。

cues.en: So with that in mind, I wanna show you how this beta coefficient can be scale-dependent.
cues.zh: 記著這個，現在示範 beta 係數如何依賴尺度。

cues.en: So let's say, so I'm making up this number here.
cues.zh: 這個數字是我編的。

cues.en: Let's say the beta coefficient here, beta one, is 1.67 in hours.
cues.zh: 假設以小時衡量時，beta1 是 1.67。

cues.en: But you know, hours is not the only unit of measuring the passage of time.
cues.zh: 但小時並不是量測時間流逝的唯一單位。

cues.en: We could also convert the data into minutes.
cues.zh: 也能把資料換算成分鐘。

cues.en: Now, we're not changing the actual data.
cues.zh: 沒有改變實際資料。

cues.en: We're not changing how the world works.
cues.zh: 沒有改變世界的運作。

cues.en: We're not going back and changing the exam scores.
cues.zh: 也沒有回去修改考試分數。

cues.en: All we're doing is recoding the hours to be in minutes.
cues.zh: 只是把小時重新編碼成分鐘。

cues.en: But that actually changes the beta coefficient.
cues.zh: 但這會改變 beta 係數。

cues.en: So now beta one is gonna be 10 instead of .167.
cues.zh: 現在 beta1 會變成 10，而不是 0.167。

cues.en: And you know, we could've done this in seconds, and now beta one all of a sudden is gonna be 600.
cues.zh: 也可以用秒，beta1 突然就會變成 600。

cues.en: So you can see there's a huge amount of variability.
cues.zh: 所以數值的變化非常大。

cues.en: There's four orders of magnitude difference between this beta coefficient and this beta coefficient.
cues.zh: 這個 beta 係數與這個之間，相差四個數量級。

cues.en: So that already tells us that these raw unstandardized beta coefficients can be difficult to interpret on their own.
cues.zh: 這已經說明，原始、未標準化的 beta 係數，很難單獨解讀。

cues.en: So you know, it's not possible just to look at a beta value and say, "Well, it's greater than one, so let's call that meaningful," you know?
cues.zh: 不能只看 beta 值，說「大於 1，所以有意義」。

cues.en: It doesn't work like that.
cues.zh: 不是這樣運作。

cues.en: So it changes completely depending on the scale of the data.
cues.zh: 它會完全隨資料尺度改變。

cues.en: And then, things can get even more confusing.
cues.zh: 還可能更加混亂。

cues.en: So let's say, you know, slightly different experiment.
cues.zh: 假設稍微不同的實驗。

cues.en: Now we're looking at the roles of sleeping and eating on exam performance.
cues.zh: 現在研究睡眠與飲食對考試表現的影響。

cues.en: So now h is the number of calories that you consume before the exam.
cues.zh: h 現在表示考試前攝取的熱量。

cues.en: So now we might find that that beta two now, which corresponds to calories, is .0051.
cues.zh: 可能發現，現在對應熱量的 beta2 是 0.0051。

cues.en: So now, how can we compare this beta value to any of these beta values?
cues.zh: 如何把這個 beta 值，與其他這些 beta 值比較？

cues.en: You know, if we had time in seconds and calories, do we say that the effect of eating is tiny because this beta value is way, way, way smaller
cues.zh: 如果時間用秒，另一個用熱量，能因為這個 beta 值遠遠小於

cues.en: than this beta value?
cues.zh: 那個，就說飲食的效果很小嗎？

cues.en: Even that question just doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 這個問題本身都沒有意義。

cues.en: We're trying to compare seconds with calories.
cues.zh: 我們在比較秒與熱量。

cues.en: It's apples and oranges.
cues.zh: 就像拿蘋果比橘子。

cues.en: So yeah, you can't do this.
cues.zh: 所以不能這樣做。

cues.en: Okay, so what I'm doing here in this slide is highlighting two difficulties of interpreting beta coefficients when they are unstandardized.
cues.zh: 這張投影片凸顯了未標準化 beta 係數的兩個解讀困難。

cues.en: So let me summarize that here.
cues.zh: 這裡整理一下。

cues.en: Unstandardized beta coefficients change depending on the scale of the data.
cues.zh: 未標準化 beta 係數會隨資料尺度改變。

cues.en: Furthermore, these unstandardized beta coefficients can be difficult, or impossible, to compare across variables, and not to mention, comparing across different studies.
cues.zh: 此外，跨變數可能很難，甚至無法比較，更不用說跨研究。

cues.en: And so these two difficulties motivate a standardization of beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 這兩個困難，帶出了 beta 係數標準化的動機。

cues.en: So let me show you what the standardization means, and then I will show you how we can interpret it.
cues.zh: 先示範標準化的意思，再說如何解讀。

cues.en: So standardization means that we have the same beta coefficients regardless of the original units of the data.
cues.zh: 標準化表示，不論資料原始單位為何，都有相同 beta 係數。

cues.en: So now all of these beta coefficients are standardized.
cues.zh: 現在這些 beta 係數全部標準化。

cues.en: So the units of s, of time spent sleeping, don't matter.
cues.zh: s，也就是睡眠時間的單位，不再重要。

cues.en: And also now, we've normalized calories and time to be in the same unit.
cues.zh: 也把熱量與時間正規化成相同單位。

cues.en: So now, actually, when you look at this table, this is telling us that the effect of calories is stronger than the effect of sleep.
cues.zh: 現在看這張表，可以知道熱量的效果比睡眠強。

cues.en: So you know, your exam performance is more strongly affected by what you eat compared to how much you sleep.
cues.zh: 考試表現受飲食的影響，比睡眠量更大。

cues.en: That's what these coefficients are telling us here, even though it looked completely the opposite in, you know, the unstandardized beta coefficients a few slides ago.
cues.zh: 這是這些係數告訴我們的，即使幾張投影片之前的未標準化係數，看起來完全相反。

cues.en: Okay, so little bit of an interim summary so far.
cues.zh: 先做個階段性整理。

cues.en: Unstandardized beta coefficients are in the scales of two data streams.
cues.zh: 未標準化 beta 係數，涉及兩串資料的尺度。

cues.en: We have the IV and the DV.
cues.zh: 自變數與依變數。

cues.en: And furthermore, each beta coefficient has a different independent variable.
cues.zh: 而且各 beta 係數對應不同自變數。

cues.en: And so those scales can also be quite different.
cues.zh: 所以尺度可能差異很大。

cues.en: Now, sometimes, this can facilitate interpretation.
cues.zh: 有時反而方便解讀。

cues.en: So if you wanna know, you know, how much better will I do on my exam for every extra 30 minutes that I'm sleeping, now, you know, you can certainly imagine
cues.zh: 如果想知道，每多睡 30 分鐘，考試會好多少，當然可以想像，

cues.en: that's a relevant number to know.
cues.zh: 這是一個值得知道的數字。

cues.en: That would be a case where the unstandardized coefficients actually facilitate interpretation.
cues.zh: 這時未標準化係數就讓解讀更容易。

cues.en: But these unstandardized terms can also stymie or, you know, impede the comparison across different variables, different models,
cues.zh: 但也可能阻礙不同變數、模型，

cues.en: different data sets, different researchers, and so on.
cues.zh: 資料集、研究者之間的比較。

cues.en: Okay, so that motivates standardized beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 因此需要標準化 beta 係數。

cues.en: So the idea of standardized beta coefficients is that they are in standard deviation units.
cues.zh: 標準化 beta 係數，以標準差為單位。

cues.en: So standard deviation units are unrelated to the scales of the original beta.
cues.zh: 標準差單位，與原始 beta 的尺度無關。

cues.en: So that's how we normalize time in different measures of time and calories, and we can directly compare time versus calories because they're all in standard deviation units.
cues.zh: 所以可以正規化不同時間單位與熱量，直接比較時間與熱量，因為都用標準差單位。

cues.en: Now, just to point out quickly, neither of these things is correct or incorrect.
cues.zh: 快速指出，兩者沒有哪個正確或錯誤。

cues.en: Neither is necessarily better or worse.
cues.zh: 也不一定哪個較好或較差。

cues.en: Sometimes you would prefer unstandardized.
cues.zh: 有時會偏好未標準化。

cues.en: Sometimes you would prefer standardized.
cues.zh: 有時偏好標準化。

cues.en: And importantly, this standardization has no effect on the inferential statistics.
cues.zh: 重要的是，標準化不影響推論統計。

cues.en: So it doesn't change the overall F value of the regression model.
cues.zh: 不會改變迴歸模型整體 F 值。

cues.en: It doesn't change the R squared.
cues.zh: 不會改變 R 平方。

cues.en: It doesn't change the statistical significance, so the P values and the T values corresponding to each beta term.
cues.zh: 也不改變統計顯著性，包括各 beta 項的 P 值與 t 值。

cues.en: The only thing it changes is the interpretation of this beta.
cues.zh: 唯一改變的是 beta 的解讀。

cues.en: Okay, so how do you actually do this?
cues.zh: 實際上如何做？

cues.en: How do you standardize these regressors?
cues.zh: 如何標準化這些迴歸係數？

cues.en: The general idea is to normalize the betas so that they have a variance equal to one.
cues.zh: 一般概念是正規化 beta，讓它們的變異數等於 1。

cues.en: So it's very similar to z-score normalization.
cues.zh: 很類似 Z 分數正規化。

cues.en: Now, there's two methods to do this.
cues.zh: 有兩種方法。

cues.en: There are two methods to standardize, to get standardized beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 兩種取得標準化 beta 係數的方法。

cues.en: Method one is to z-normalize basically the entire data set.
cues.zh: 第一種，基本上對整份資料集做 Z 標準化。

cues.en: You z-normalize the dependent variable and all of the independent variables before you actually run the regression.
cues.zh: 真正執行迴歸之前，先對依變數與所有自變數做 Z 標準化。

cues.en: So before you even get to the stage of modeling, you z-score all of the columns of the data set individually.
cues.zh: 甚至還沒建模，就先把資料集的各欄，分別轉成 Z 分數。

cues.en: And so then, in that case, the beta values are still technically in the units of the data, but now the units of the data
cues.zh: 這種情況，beta 值技術上仍是資料的單位，但資料單位現在

cues.en: are standard deviations.
cues.zh: 是標準差。

cues.en: So in this case, the standardized regression coefficients and the unstandardized regression coefficients are both in exactly the same scale.
cues.zh: 所以標準化與未標準化迴歸係數，現在會處於完全相同尺度。

cues.en: Okay, so this might sound familiar, z-normalizing.
cues.zh: Z 標準化可能很熟悉。

cues.en: I mentioned this earlier in context with the intercept.
cues.zh: 之前談截距時提過。

cues.en: There I said, if you zero center, if you mean center all of the data values, the DV and all of the IVs,
cues.zh: 當時說，執行迴歸之前，如果把依變數與全部自變數的資料值，

cues.en: before running the regression model, that's the one case where you don't need an intercept.
cues.zh: 全部平均中心化，那就是不需要截距的情況。

cues.en: So this is just a bit similar to that, because when we z-normalize, you also get rid of the mean.
cues.zh: 這有點相似，因為 Z 標準化也會移除平均值。

cues.en: Okay, so that's one method.
cues.zh: 這是第一種方法。

cues.en: We have another method, which is to leave the data in their original scales.
cues.zh: 第二種方法，把資料留在原始尺度。

cues.en: So we don't do anything to the data.
cues.zh: 完全不改資料。

cues.en: And then we change the beta values.
cues.zh: 再改 beta 值。

cues.en: We recompute the beta values by standardizing them according to, now we need to consider the standard deviations both of the independent variable and the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 重新計算 beta 值來標準化，現在必須同時考慮自變數與依變數的標準差。

cues.en: So that formula is this.
cues.zh: 公式如下。

cues.en: So we have the unstandardized, so the raw beta coefficient, times the standard deviation of the independent variable
cues.zh: 取未標準化，也就是原始 beta 係數，乘上對應參數的

cues.en: for the corresponding parameter.
cues.zh: 自變數標準差。

cues.en: So this would be independent variable k.
cues.zh: 這裡是自變數 k。

cues.en: So data x.
cues.zh: 也就是資料 X。

cues.en: And then divided by the standard deviation of the data, y.
cues.zh: 再除以資料 Y 的標準差。

cues.en: So you can see we're normalizing by the standard deviation of the DV and the relevant IV.
cues.zh: 可以看到，利用依變數與對應自變數的標準差，來做正規化。

cues.en: And sometimes people would call this the letter b instead of beta for the standardized coefficient.
cues.zh: 有時人們會用字母 b，而不是 beta，表示標準化係數。

cues.en: You don't see this super often, but sometimes people do this.
cues.zh: 不常見，但有時會這樣。

cues.en: Now, fortunately, you don't actually need to do this yourself.
cues.zh: 幸好，其實不必自己做。

cues.en: Most statistical software packages will do this for you.
cues.zh: 大部分統計軟體套件會代勞。

cues.en: They will output a regression table that includes both the standardized and the unstandardized regression coefficients.
cues.zh: 輸出的迴歸表，會同時包含標準化與未標準化係數。

cues.en: Okay, so now, the last thing I want to discuss here is how that changes the interpretation of these beta values.
cues.zh: 最後想討論，這如何改變 beta 值的解讀。

cues.en: So you now know, because you've seen it in the previous video and in this video, how exactly to interpret these beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 上一支與這支影片，已經看到如何確切解讀 beta 係數。

cues.en: That was for the raw beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 那是針對原始 beta。

cues.en: What I would like you to do now is pause the video and see if you can come up with a precise definition of the standardized beta coefficient.
cues.zh: 現在請暫停影片，試著提出標準化 beta 係數的精確定義。

cues.en: So how exactly do you interpret a beta coefficient when it's standardized?
cues.zh: beta 標準化之後，究竟如何解讀？

cues.en: Okay, have you figured it out yet?
cues.zh: 想出來了嗎？

cues.en: So the answer is that it's almost exactly the same.
cues.zh: 答案是，幾乎完全相同。

cues.en: So this is text that I copied from the previous video.
cues.zh: 這是從上一支影片複製的文字。

cues.en: Really similar.
cues.zh: 非常相似。

cues.en: So beta two, as an example, reflects the effect of...
cues.zh: 例如，beta2 反映的是……

cues.en: Now, it's no longer one-unit change in x, like if this were food, then this would be calories, one calorie.
cues.zh: 現在不再是 X 改變一個原始單位；如果是食物，就會是熱量，一大卡。

cues.en: It's not one-unit change.
cues.zh: 不是一個原始單位的變化。

cues.en: It is one-standard deviation change in x.
cues.zh: 而是 X 改變一個標準差。

cues.en: And that is pretty interesting, because the number of calories that one standard deviation corresponds to depends on the data set.
cues.zh: 這很有趣，因為一個標準差對應多少熱量，取決於資料集。

cues.en: So that can actually vary.
cues.zh: 所以實際數值可以改變。

cues.en: So one-standard deviation change in h, and how much does that change y?
cues.zh: h 改變一個標準差，會讓 y 改變多少？

cues.en: So in the example I showed, so in the numbers I made up a few slides ago, I said that beta two equals .8.
cues.zh: 前面編的數字中，beta2 等於 0.8。

cues.en: So that would mean that for every standard deviation of increase in food that you eat before you take the exam,
cues.zh: 表示每當考試前吃的食物量，增加一個標準差，

cues.en: that gives you .8 standard deviations a higher score on your exam.
cues.zh: 考試分數就提高 0.8 個標準差。

cues.en: Okay, and then, you know, we still need to, for multiple regression, we still need to keep this in mind, when all other variables are held constant.
cues.zh: 對多元迴歸，仍必須記得其他所有變數保持固定這個條件。

cues.en: But the main thing to point out here is that it's the beta coefficients, the standardized beta coefficients are now one-standard deviation change in the independent variable,
cues.zh: 主要重點是，標準化 beta 係數，現在表示自變數改變一個標準差，

cues.en: and what is the standard deviation change in the dependent variable?
cues.zh: 依變數會改變多少個標準差。

cues.en: Okay, so that was a pretty fun video.
cues.zh: 這支影片相當有趣。

cues.en: I hope you enjoyed it.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡。

cues.en: You learned more about interpreting and working with regression coefficients, and in particular, how to interpret standardized and unstandardized coefficients,
cues.zh: 學到了如何解讀與使用迴歸係數，尤其是標準化與未標準化係數的解讀，

cues.en: and the two methods for standardizing them.
cues.zh: 以及兩種標準化方法。
